heading: Token
text:
### Token [IRET.7.1]

A token is one partial match travelling the beta network: the facts
bound so far, one per LHS pattern position, in pattern order.

| Field | Holds |
|---|---|
| fact_count | how many pattern positions are bound |
| facts | the bound facts, indexed by pattern position |
| creation_timetag | a monotonic stamp; this is what orders the agenda ([LDET.5.5]) |
| hash | a cached hash of the fact-id tuple |
| next | links the token into a beta memory |

Three of these are performance decisions with observable consequences.
The **timetag** is not a timestamp — it is a stamp monotone in completion
order, compared as [LDET.5.5] defines, so agenda order is deterministic and
independent of the clock. The **hash
is cached** because a token is hashed far more often than it is built,
and it is over the fact-id *tuple*, so two tokens binding the same facts
in the same positions hash alike. The **list link is intrusive**, so
adding a token to a beta memory allocates nothing.

idris.note: A token: the facts bound so far, one per positive pattern, in pattern order. Its identity is the tuple [IRET.11.3]; its timetag is a function of the tuple (`ldet_5_5__before`), so it is not stored -- the reading of [LDET.5.5] in which a timetag is derived from the matched facts, not assigned. The hash pre-filter and the intrusive link are representation.
